title: Exact Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion for Unital Qubit Channels
abstract: We study when a noisy qubit channel renders all positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) jointly measurable. For every unital qubit channel, we derive the exact incompatibility-breaking criterion and prove that projective measurements already determine the boundary for arbitrary POVMs. Through the steering--joint-measurability correspondence, this result gives the exact POVM-steering boundary for all two-qubit states with maximally mixed marginals, with the Werner states recovered as a special case. For nonunital qubit channels, we construct a generally asymmetric parent POVM and obtain an explicit sufficient incompatibility-breaking condition, which in turn yields a sufficient unsteerability criterion for arbitrary two-qubit states.
summary: This paper establishes exact criteria for when noisy qubit channels preserve the ability to perform all possible measurements (POVMs). By linking this concept to state steering and joint measurability, the authors provide rigorous bounds on channel noise and characterize unsteerable two-qubit states. It is a highly theoretical contribution advancing the understanding of quantum resource limitations.
main_problem: The central problem is deriving the exact criterion determining when a noisy quantum channel renders all Positive-Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) jointly measurable, which relates to incompatibility breaking.
main_result: For unital qubit channels, the paper proves that POVM-incompatibility breaking coincides exactly with PVM-incompatibility breaking. It also provides sufficient criteria for nonunital channels and unsteerability of two-qubit states.
method: The authors employ a dual framework using support functions, relating joint measurability to steering problems via the steering–joint-measurability correspondence. They use SDP techniques and geometric arguments (like Lemma 1) to establish necessary and sufficient conditions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on qubit channels ($N$), modeled by CPTP maps, and their effect on joint measurability of POVMs ($\{M_a\}$). The results are extended to characterize unsteerability for two-qubit states ($ho_{AB}$).
key_observables: The diagnostic parameters include the integral $\int_{S^2} \|D\hat{n}\| d\mu(\hat{n})$ for unital channels, and the expectation value of a Hermitian witness $	ext{Tr}(Hho)$ for state separability/unsteerability.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on whether the channel is unital or nonunital, characterized by parameters like $D$ (noise matrix) and $\vec{t}$ (nonunitality vector).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include relying on strong duality in SDP (Slater's condition) and establishing correspondences between different types of quantum resource limitations (e.g., steering $\leftrightarrow$ joint measurability).
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail mathematical derivations involving geometric inequalities and explicit construction of parent POVMs ($\Pi_{D,\vec{t}}$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining general compatibility criteria using SDP (Appendix A), establishing a correspondence between joint measurability and steering (Section B.2), deriving the exact criterion for unital channels (Theorem 1), and finally providing sufficient conditions for nonunital channels and unsteerability of two-qubit states (Theorem 2).
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental, rigorous mathematical tools to quantify how much noise a quantum channel can tolerate before it fundamentally alters the set of measurable physical operations, which is crucial for understanding decoherence in quantum computation.
